scenario: AITA for dumping food on my girlfriends plate at a wedding until it was overflowing? | Me and my girlfriend are moderately overweight. We have been noticing that we were getting fatter still, so I pushed us to try and lose some weight. I'm mainly the one trying to keep us on track and very often I have to call her out when she's sliding back into our old eating habits. So this last weekend we went to a wedding together as guests. She just kind of stared at it, then got up and went outside alone. Everyone was staring at me at this point and I thought it was better I just went outside too to talk to her. She told me she was humiliated and that I stepped out of line and they I came off as a controlling jerk. So, am I the asshole for taking a stand against her completely disregard for our agreed upon diet?

prediction.raw: 1. I think you are the asshole in this situation. While it's understandable that you're trying to support your girlfriend in her weight loss journey, your approach was completely wrong. Dumping food on her plate until it was overflowing was a humiliating and controlling behavior, especially in a public setting like a wedding. It's one thing to have a private conversation with your girlfriend about her eating habits, but it's another thing to publicly shame her in front of your families. Your actions came across as condescending and judgmental, rather than supportive. Instead of trying to police her food intake, you could have had a gentle and respectful conversation with her about your concerns. You could have also tried to find ways to support her in her weight loss journey that don't involve publicly embarrassing her. It's also worth considering that everyone has different relationships with food, and it's possible that your girlfriend was just trying to enjoy herself at the wedding. It's not about completely disregarding your agreed-upon diet, but about finding balance and allowing for occasional indulgences. Overall, your behavior was not only hurtful to your girlfriend, but it also damaged your relationship and made you look like a controlling jerk in front of your families. A more empathetic and supportive approach would have been much more effective in addressing your concerns.
